{'translation': 'The chairman of the independent committee, Luk Kai-hong, said at the opening that written submissions had been received from eight parties involved, and government representatives would make their submissions tomorrow.'}

{'translation': 'Government submissions exceed 400 pages'}

{'translation': "The chairman of the independent committee, Luk Kai-hong, said at the opening that written submissions had been received from eight parties involved, including the SAR government, the Competition Commission, nine residents, the new management committee of the Wang Fuk Court owners' corporation, ISS Property Management Company, Wang Tai Fire Engineering Company, and Leung Ping-kee, director of Chung Wah Development Company. Among them, Wang Tai and the new management committee of the Wang Fuk Court owners' corporation will only submit written submissions. The submissions from six of the parties involved have been uploaded to the independent committee's website, and other submissions will be uploaded in succession before the hearings begin over the next two days."}

{'translation': "Luk Kai-hong pointed out that the government representative's submission alone exceeded 400 pages, while the new management committee representative's submission was over 100 pages. The parties would not read out the contents paragraph by paragraph during the hearings. The committee and the lawyers of each representative would summarise matters related to the fire and the roles of different stakeholders during the final three-day hearing, and put forward recommendations for improvement."}

{'translation': 'ISS Property submission: Extreme sorrow'}

{'translation': "The representative of ISS Property, barrister Ho Cheuk-hang, made submissions first, expressing extreme sorrow over the tragedy, and said they would listen with an open mind to evidence from all parties, including expert evidence and constructive recommendations, hoping to consider areas for improvement through the investigation to prevent similar incidents from happening again. Ho Cheuk-hang pointed out that ISS had not been appointed as any consultant or supervisory role in the major repair works of Wang Fuk Court, nor had it charged additional fees for services assisting the major repair works, and that there were limited follow-up actions it could take regarding residents' complaints about the major repair works, including smoking issues."}

{'translation': 'On workers smoking: Can only advise, no enforcement power'}

{'translation': 'ISS had raised the smoking issue with the contractors Wang Yip and engineering consultants Hung Ngai, and had also put up no-smoking notices in the estate. When staff witnessed workers smoking, they had also shouted to stop them, but ISS could only advise and had no enforcement power.'}

{'translation': 'Regarding the main fire switch being turned off, the representative of ISS, barrister Ho Cheuk-hang, pointed out that "although it was regrettable that (electrician) Master Lo was careless", he believed the committee should fully consider the actual situation of the fire alarm system failure, including why Chung Wah Development was not present when the water tank was drained. (File photo)'}

{'translation': 'Pointed out no contractors present when water tank was drained, Chung Wah Development nowhere to be seen'}

{'translation': 'Ho said that management office staff coordinated with two fire service installation contractors, and the management office staff issued work orders at the request of Wang Yip, with electrician Lo Kwok-sui assisting Wang Yip in draining the fire water tank. Ho said that if a registered fire service contractor had been present to assist during the draining, the work "would not have been a problem in itself", saying "ISS had no reason to suspect that Wang Yip would not invite a registered fire service contractor to be present", but "unfortunately, when the water was being drained, no contractors were present, and the Chung Wah Development works commissioned by Wang Yip were nowhere to be seen."'}

{'translation': 'Why was no one aware the main fire switch had been turned off?'}

{'translation': 'Ho Cheuk-hang pointed out that "although it was regrettable that Master Lo was careless", he believed the committee should fully consider the actual situation of the fire alarm system failure, including why Chung Wah Development was not present when the water was drained, and why no one discovered the main fire switch had been turned off during the three months between the draining and the fire. He also pointed out that if the latest version of the fire service installation code had been followed, he believed the accident of the switch being turned off "would very likely not have happened."'}

{'translation': 'Accused Wang Tai Fire\'s Chung Kit-man of "talking nonsense"'}

{'translation': 'Ho, during his submissions, criticised that if a representative of Chung Wah Development Engineering Company had been present, Lo Kwok-sui would not have accidentally turned off the "switch". He also questioned the claim by Chung Kit-man, director of Wang Tai Fire Engineering Company, that he had sought a Shutdown Notice (SDN) from ISS property officer Cheng Tsz-ying, saying the phone record evidence he presented was "completely untrustworthy nonsense".'}

{'translation': "In addition, Ho also raised the question of why the fuses of the fire alarm systems in the seven buildings had been broken. At this point, Luk Kai-hong questioned that if the fuses had been broken before the fire, how to explain that the fire alarms in two of the buildings had sounded during the fire. Ho Cheuk-hang believed this issue required study, pointing out that Wang Chi House was not affected by the fire, but its fuses were also broken, meaning that regardless of whether the switch was turned off or not, the alarm in Wang Chi House would not have sounded. On the other hand, Ho Cheuk-hang pointed out that property management companies could take measures to make the voting process at owners' meetings fairer, but ISS had no legal power to implement committee recommendations. He said that if the Building Management Ordinance could be amended in this regard, property management companies could be given the power to monitor the fairness of voting."}

{'translation': "In the final part of his submissions, Ho Cheuk-hang reiterated that ISS management staff and the engineering officer had tried their best to urge residents to leave and attempted to activate the fire alarms after the fire broke out. After seeing the alarms had failed, the engineering officer also ran to the pump rooms of the two buildings to turn on the electrical switches, at least causing the alarms in Wang Tao House and Wang Sun House to sound briefly. Ho pointed out that ISS staff did their best to assist in evacuation, even disregarding their own safety, staying until the last moment before leaving the estate, and continuing to assist affected residents after evacuating to the community hall. He said that while the tragedy was painful, it also reflected the contributions of many people, including the most important firefighters, as well as frontline staff of the property management company. ISS would humbly accept the committee's recommendations."}

{'translation': 'Barrister Chan Chi-lung (left) and barrister Kwan Yau-lai (right) representing Chung Wah Development Engineering Company.'}

{'translation': '"Chung Wah Development" pointed out there were other factors besides the alarm bell...'}

{'translation': 'Chung Wah Development, a fire service contractor that had applied 85 times to the Fire Services Department for extensions to close the fire service system during the major repair works, its director Leung Ping-kee had earlier admitted that he had never visited the site for inspection. Leung\'s representative, barrister Chan Chi-lung, said that Ho Kin-yip, director of Wang Yip, had always told Leung Ping-kee that Wang Yip was a fire service contractor. Leung had also checked the register of fire service contractors and found "Wang Yip" on it, so he sincerely believed that Wang Yip was indeed a registered fire service contractor, even though this was later confirmed to be untrue. Moreover, Chung Wah Development had previously cooperated with Wang Yip on other projects, so it believed there would be no major problems with the Wang Fuk Court project. Phone records also showed that Leung Ping-kee had spoken 85 times with a Mr Cheung, a site supervisor of Wang Yip.'}

{'translation': 'Luk Kai-hong: I find this argument rather hard to accept'}

{'translation': 'Leung Ping-kee agreed that if the fire alarm system had been effective during the fire, it might have reduced casualties, but reminded the committee to consider other factors, including the inter-departmental expert panel\'s view that residents had no more than 10 minutes to escape. Luk Kai-hong questioned, "Don\'t tell me the fire alarm is useless... If you say that, I don\'t think anyone here will agree with you."'}

{'translation': 'Chan said "absolutely not", and was merely raising other factors for the committee\'s reference. Luk Kai-hong said that if the alarm had sounded earlier, "even residents two floors higher (could have escaped)", and bluntly stated that if Leung hoped to use this to reduce his responsibility, "I find this argument rather hard to accept". Chan reiterated that Leung agreed the fire alarm was useful, and expressed deep remorse and apology for the incident, hoping that those affected would recover from the trauma soon.'}
